newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish court rejects US filmmaker's damages suit.
newsitem.headline: Danish court rejects US filmmaker's damages suit.

text.p: A Danish court on Friday dismissed a damages claim brought by Oscar-winning U.S. film director Sydney Pollack against Danish state television for screening one of his films in a drastically reduced format.
Pollack, championed in Denmark by the Danish Film Directors' Association, brought a suit claiming 100,000 crowns ($15,600) for alleged damage to his professional reputation.

The association, supported by the European Directors' Guild and the Hollywood-based Artists' Rights Foundation, backed Pollack in the hope of winning greater legal protection against pan scanning films screened on television.
The court ruling said that although Pollack's artistic rights had been violated by the cuts in the film format, the wording of the contract with Danish Radio effectively deprived him of his rights.

The case involved the television broadcast in 1991 of Pollack's Cinemascope film "Three Days of the Condor" in a pan scanned version, a technique which in adapting a film for the small screen cuts the visible picture by over 50 percent.
Pollack claimed the process erased material in the periphery of the picture frame, placed there to show lurking danger and create a mood of paranoia.
Danish State Radio claimed that the distributors, not broadcasters, determined the format of films to be televised.
Pollack, 62, won an Oscar in 1986 for "Out of Africa", starring Meryl Streep and Robert Redford and based on the book by Danish baroness Karen Blixen.
Although the copyright in "Three Days of the Condor" is owned by its producers, Danish law gives permanent rights to artists regardless of subsequent ownership of their work.
The ruling by three judges was unanimous. The Danish Film Directors' Association said it would consult Pollack before deciding whether to appeal. ($ = 6.376 Danish Crowns)
